claim: COVID-19 is the disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2; SC2).
source: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is the disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2; SC2), which has caused a worldwide pandemic with striking morbidity and mortality.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the causative agent of COVID-19.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 has caused a worldwide pandemic with striking morbidity and mortality.
source: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is the disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2; SC2), which has caused a worldwide pandemic with striking morbidity and mortality.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the global impact of COVID-19.

claim: Evaluation of SC2 strains demonstrated impressive genetic variability.
source: Evaluation of SC2 strains demonstrated impressive genetic variability, and many of these viral variants are now defined as variants of concern (VOC) that cause enhanced transmissibility, decreased susceptibility to antibody neutralization or therapeutics, and/or the ability to induce severe disease.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about SARS-CoV-2 evolution.

claim: Many SC2 viral variants are defined as variants of concern (VOC) that cause enhanced transmissibility, decreased susceptibility to antibody neutralization or therapeutics, and/or the ability to induce severe disease.
source: Evaluation of SC2 strains demonstrated impressive genetic variability, and many of these viral variants are now defined as variants of concern (VOC) that cause enhanced transmissibility, decreased susceptibility to antibody neutralization or therapeutics, and/or the ability to induce severe disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the characteristics of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern.

claim: The delta and omicron variants are particularly problematic based on their impressive and unprecedented transmissibility and ability to cause breakthrough infections.
source: Currently, the delta (δ) and omicron (ο) variants are particularly problematic based on their impressive and unprecedented transmissibility and ability to cause breakthrough infections.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the characteristics of delta and omicron variants.

claim: The delta variant accumulates at high concentrations in host tissues.
source: The delta variant also accumulates at high concentrations in host tissues and has caused waves of lethal disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the delta variant's behavior.

claim: The delta variant has caused waves of lethal disease.
source: The delta variant also accumulates at high concentrations in host tissues and has caused waves of lethal disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the clinical impact of the delta variant.

claim: CHI3L1 stimulates ACE2 and Spike (S) priming proteases that mediate SC2 infection.
source: Because studies from our laboratory have demonstrated that chitinase 3-like-1 (CHI3L1) stimulates ACE2 and Spike (S) priming proteases that mediate SC2 infection, studies were undertaken to determine if interventions that target CHI3L1 are effective inhibitors of SC2 viral variant infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: CHI3L1 augments epithelial cell infection by pseudoviruses that express the alpha, beta, gamma, delta, or omicron S proteins.
source: Here, we demonstrate that CHI3L1 augments epithelial cell infection by pseudoviruses that express the alpha, beta, gamma, delta, or omicron S proteins and that the CHI3L1 inhibitors anti-CHI3L1 and kasugamycin inhibit epithelial cell infection by these VOC pseudovirus moieties.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CHI3L1 inhibitors anti-CHI3L1 and kasugamycin inhibit epithelial cell infection by alpha, beta, gamma, delta, and omicron VOC pseudovirus moieties.
source: Here, we demonstrate that CHI3L1 augments epithelial cell infection by pseudoviruses that express the alpha, beta, gamma, delta, or omicron S proteins and that the CHI3L1 inhibitors anti-CHI3L1 and kasugamycin inhibit epithelial cell infection by these VOC pseudovirus moieties.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CHI3L1 is a universal, VOC-independent therapeutic target in COVID-19.
source: Thus, CHI3L1 is a universal, VOC-independent therapeutic target in COVID-19.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing CHI3L1's role across multiple variants.

claim: COVID-19 was first discovered in man in 2019.
